explanation: Genetic disorders are medical conditions resulting from alleles inherited from parents. An autosome is any chromosome other than a sex chromosome (X or Y). Genetic disorders caused by genes on autosomes are called autosomal disorders. Autosomal dominant disorders occur in individuals with genotype AA or Aa, while those with genotype aa are unaffected. Autosomal recessive disorders only occur in individuals with genotype aa; individuals with AA are unaffected, and heterozygotes (Aa) are unaffected carriers.

questions.q: How do autosomal dominant and autosomal recessive genotypes differ in terms of disease expression?
opts: Autosomal dominant disorders affect only homozygous recessive individuals; autosomal recessive affect heterozygotes.
Autosomal dominant disorders affect AA and Aa individuals; autosomal recessive disorders affect only aa individuals.
Autosomal dominant disorders affect only females; autosomal recessive affect only males.
Autosomal dominant disorders require two copies of the allele; autosomal recessive require one copy.
